newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open stronger on relief after data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open stronger on relief after data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened stronger on Wednesday but underperformed their U.S. counterparts as fixed-income markets in both countries rallied on the release of tame U.S. economic data.

"The data this morning in the U.S. was more of a relief than anything else, a little bit softer than expected," said David Adamo, managing director of fixed-income research with Scotia Capital Markets. "We outperformed on the way down, so underperforming on the way up isn't much of a surprise."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.57 to C$118.62 to yield 6.567 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 30/32 full point to yield 6.60 percent. The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to three basis point from eight basis points at Tuesday's close.
Fixed-income markets in both countries strengthened after the U.S. Labor Department said the producer price index fell 0.1 percent in July, compared with expectations of a 0.1 percent rise.
Markets also benefitted from a report that U.S. retail sales rose 0.6 percent in July, below expectations of a 0.7 percent rise.
The reports also helped the Canadian dollar rally below C$1.39 (US$0.7194), which helped dampen speculation of a near-term Bank of Canada rate hike.

"I'm not sure how long we're going to be here for but we are up right now. There is a good potential over the next 24 hours for the market to trade lower," said Adamo. "On rallies now, from a technical standpoint, you would expect to see a little bit of selling."
Analysts said the market is now looking ahead to the release tomorrow of the U.S. consumer price index for July.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.08 to C$108.38 to yield 6.099 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.40 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 30 basis points from 32 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange fell 0.08 to 119.00 with 2846 contracts changing hands.
